chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the first person for whom the coffin (na'ash) was made, so he said: Fatima (peace be upon her).

key_terms.النَّعْشُ: Casket or coffin used for carrying the deceased to burial
key_terms.فَاطِمَةُ: Fatima, daughter of the Prophet Muhammad

ai.seo_question: Who was the first person for whom a coffin was made according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies Sayyida Fatima al-Zahra (peace be upon her) as the first person for whom a *na'ash* (coffin) was constructed, a detail often cited in Shia historiography to emphasize her unique status and the early establishment of funeral rites for the Ahl al-Bayt. This attribution underscores the reverence accorded to her by the Imams and serves as a theological marker of her precedence in the spiritual hierarchy of the Prophet's household.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the first one for whom the casket (coffin) was made to be. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘ Syeda Fatima<sup>asws</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “I asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘
Who was the initiator of coffins for deceased people?’ He replied, ‘Fatimah, ‘Alayha al-Salam, was the one.’”
